local_rejection: The original implementation passed one explicitly selected ignored test under a five-second timeout and strace EINTR injection. Trace /tmp/martensite-sleep-original-eintr.trace shows exactly six clock_nanosleep(CLOCK_REALTIME, 0, request, NULL) calls, each injected EINTR and no retry. injection_safety: The original calls use a null remainder pointer. Do not reuse synthetic EINTR injection on a candidate that assumes initialized remainder output on interruption; the injector does not populate it. This is syscall-rejection evidence, not an actual delivered-signal or pthread-cancellation test.
unnamed_error_fixture: The additional ignored GNU/Linux fixture passed explicitly (one test) under a five-second timeout with strace error=4094 injection. Trace /tmp/martensite-sleep-original-unnamed.trace records exactly two zero-duration clock_nanosleep calls with NULL remainder, each returning injected errno 4094. Both entry points preserved that raw value. Unlike incoming sentinel 12345, 4094 is within the Linux syscall error range and is not a named nix errno variant.

limits: Native run 38988376147 at 2317cc2 exposed an incorrect cross-platform fixture: macOS zero-duration sleep left errno 60 (ETIMEDOUT), not incoming zero (#155). Apple UNIX03 nanosleep returns success after a timed wait without restoring ETIMEDOUT. The corrected fixtures separate GNU/Linux preservation from macOS timeout errno; corrected native gates remain pending. Cancellation and replacement compatibility remain unverified. No permanent exception is proposed; Windows is unchanged and excluded.
